rows: That is a different offer. The answer to that one is no.
Brawling costs money. Whoever pays for it should know the figure before the bell.
Nerve is a price. I want to see the figure before I pay it.
Pace is leverage. I do not give leverage away, and I do not lend it.
The people are the ones who pay most in this building. They deserve a straight figure.
My position is set, and it does not move for a comment from the floor.
My position is secured by leverage I have built. I am not going to hand it over.
Take the stance as a figure. It is the stance of someone who reads the small print before the signature.
Technique is a line item. Name a price for it, and I will tell you what it is worth to me.
Strikes come at a cost. Nothing beyond the price is on the table.
A risk I did not choose is not a risk I will carry. Make it yours, or drop it.
A stall is a slow leak in the deal, and I do not let them run.
The people deserve a contest with a clear price. I will insist the figures are shown.
You say I am irrelevant. My position is secured by leverage, and I intend to keep it.
Proud of your {strength}, fine. Name the price you want for it. Fine. Name the price you want for it, and I will answer that.
I have priced your {strength}, and it comes in below the figure you quoted.
Composed, and priced in. Well priced. Calm is cheaper than a scene, and I respect the saving.
Noted. That is a figure I can work with, and I have noted it.
I could refuse outright. I would rather name my price and leave it there.
One fall, one price. Keep me down and the room is yours. Simple as that.
On the mat, the price does not change once we start. Stay with the number.
Grounded or standing, my answer does not change without a better offer.
Stay in front of me and meet the number in full.
That answer is within the figure. It meets the price.
No figure from you yet. The room is waiting for a figure, and so am I.
Fair figure. We will settle the bill at the bell.
I will wrestle this match for the figure we discussed, and I will finish it properly.
My approach is precise. I say what I will take, and I stand by it.
Whatever happens, the books will show what was paid.
The price is not yet fixed. One line remains open.
I have one more figure to name, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
You want something that would stand up to scrutiny. Fair. I haven't got it, and I won't put a price on a claim I can't support.
A charge without evidence is a bad investment. I withdraw it. There's still a match worth having.
Good. Take that off the table. We can negotiate nothing about the result once the bell goes.
That's a fair correction. The wrestling will be the only thing that settles our contest.
The result is on the table. Let us see who can deliver what they have offered.
The audience paid for a contest, not an unverified claim. We can settle the wrestling on those terms.
An allegation has no value until it is backed up. What can this contest actually establish?
Set the claim aside. What can we deliver in the ring that the paying audience can judge?
You've priced in my {strength}. You haven't accounted for the leverage I gain when you commit to that defence.
Your plan for my {strength} carries a cost. I intend to make you pay it every time you try to take the initiative.
Fair assessment. An allegation without backing has no value on the balance sheet.
I accept the distinction. Let us deal in what we can actually deliver to the paying audience.
Experience is an asset, not a guarantee of the return. This match has its own terms.
Your years have a value. I won't agree to pay a premium until I see how you use them.
The return on experience is knowing which position is worth taking before you commit to it.
You may present a different proposition. Experience helps me recognise where the leverage lies.
You've invested time in studying me. That does not entitle you to the return you anticipated.
Your research assumes I will offer the same terms. I reserve the right to renegotiate them.
I study where control changes hands. That's where the worthwhile leverage usually lies.
My preparation is to compare the cost of each option before the pressure forces a decision.
